## Chief AI Knittakers

### Salka Sól Eyfeld

Salka Sól Eyfeld is our Chief AI Knittaker for Visit Iceland’s AI Knittakers campaign. An Icelandic singer, actress, presenter and lifelong knitter, she first learned to knit at the age of eight and still regularly meets friends to knit and socialise. Her passion for knitting has helped inspire a younger generation to pick up the needles and embrace the craft. She also co-authored UNA , a knitting book created in collaboration with Sjöfn from Stroff Knitting.

A prominent and versatile figure in Iceland’s creative scene, Salka is known for fronting the reggae band AmabAdamA, her work with Reykjavíkurdætur and her role in the acclaimed Icelandic drama Trapped . Her creative career spans music, theatre, film and television. She has composed music for theatre productions, performed on stage, appeared in films and television series, written theatrical productions and lent her voice to countless animated characters.

She has also worked with national broadcaster RÚV, served as a judge on Iceland’s The Voice and won Female Vocalist of the Year at the Icelandic Music Awards.

### Bergþór Pálsson

Bergþór Pálsson is one of Visit Iceland’s AI Knittakers. An Icelandic baritone singer, actor, voice teacher and experienced knitter, his career has spanned opera, operetta, musical theatre and stage performance, including appearances with the Icelandic Opera and as a soloist with the Iceland Symphony Orchestra.

Bergþór first learned to knit decades ago while working night shifts and later returned to the craft more seriously while performing at the National Theatre of Iceland. His projects have included traditional Icelandic waistcoats, intricately patterned sweaters, hats and handmade gifts for his family.

## Iceland Is Waiting

Thinking about visiting Iceland? Whether it’s your first trip or your fifth, there’s always something new to discover. Volcanoes, glaciers, geothermal pools, and a few surprises along the way. You might find yourself chasing the Northern Lights, soaking in a hot pool in the rain, or wondering how the landscape can change so much in just a few miles.

Whatever brings you here, there’s plenty more to explore.
